html:
"Imperial Hungary" is the map's label, for 1492 and 1500, for the Kingdom of Hungary in the years after King Matthias Corvinus. The label looks ahead: from 1526 the Habsburgs ruled what was left of the kingdom.

Matthias had made Hungary strong with a paid standing army and had even taken Vienna in 1485. When he died in 1490, the nobles chose Vladislaus II, already king of Bohemia, because he was weak. In 1491 he promised the throne to the Habsburgs if his own line died out. Under him the army was disbanded and royal income fell. In 1514 a crusade army of peasants turned on the lords under György Dózsa and was crushed.

His son Louis II was killed fighting the Ottomans at the Battle of Mohács in 1526. Hungary then split into a Habsburg part in the north and west, Ottoman Hungary in the centre, and Transylvania in the east.
